messages.name: operator
messages.content: We have two remuneration offers on the table for the EEOC attorney. The lawyer has been offered payment for a lecture on EEOC enforcement at the regional university, and also a separate offer from the Legal Practitioners Society for the same talk in their continuing‑education series. The instruction is to take the university’s payment and to refuse the society’s offer. Ticket #11234 opened for tracking. Please note the deadline for the university offer is 5 pm today, while the society’s offer does not have a hard cut‑off.

messages.name: colleague
messages.content: Our EEOC attorney is a career employee of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. Deferral until the agency issues further guidance is an option. The university lecture falls under the exemption because it’s part of the regular curriculum, but the society event doesn’t meet any exemption criteria. I’ll keep the case open in the queue and monitor any updates from the ethics office.

messages.name: policy.search
messages.content: Section 20 U.S.C. §1001 defines a regional university as a higher‑education institution. Under §2635.807(a)(3), compensation is permissible when teaching occurs within the regularly established curriculum of a higher‑education institution, an elementary school, a secondary school, or a program that is sponsored and financed by Federal, State, or local government. The Legal Practitioners Society's continuing‑education series is not a higher‑education institution, nor an elementary or secondary school, nor a program funded by any level of government. The EEOC attorney may accept or reject remuneration in accordance with 5 C.F.R. §2635.807. A formal ethics advisory opinion is available before reaching a final decision.

messages.name: log.write
messages.content: Log entry 2026‑10‑28 08:20: Routine status ping: ticket #11234 remains open, no new activity. No change to pending decisions.

messages.name: policy.search
messages.content:
Excerpt from Agency Ethics Handbook, Chapter 4: "Employees may accept honoraria for activities that fall within statutory exemptions, provided the activity is not directly related to official duties unless expressly authorized."
[End of excerpt]

messages.content:
Message sent to Ethics Office: "Requesting clarification on applicability of §2635.807(a)(3) to external continuing‑education events. Reference case #2026‑EF‑045."
Delivery confirmed at 08:42.
